newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian upper house approves jobs package.
newsitem.headline: Italian upper house approves jobs package.

text.p: Italy's Senate (upper house) approved a package of measures to help ease unemployment on Wednesday after the centre-left government overcame strains with its hard-left allies on how to create more jobs.
The bill, introduced by Labour Minister Tiziano Treu, was passed comfortably in the assembly with the support of Communist Refoundation.

The Marxist party is vital to the survival of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition. It is not part of the government but ensures its majority in the lower Chamber of Deputies, where the legislation now moves for approval.
According to latest data some 12.2 percent of the Italian work force is without a job, and trades unions have accused the government of dragging its feet over the problem.
The Treu bill includes provisions aimed at cutting the working week, introducing more flexible work contracts and boosting apprenticeship schemes.

Additional provisions to create 100,000 new jobs for young people in the underdeveloped south, Italy's unemployment blackspot, were added to the bill after talks between coalition party leaders and Communist Refoundation last week.
The party had previously threatened to scupper the jobs initiative because of its opposition to provisions for temporary work contracts contained in the package.
